## Historical audit — S0171, visible chunk 1 of 5

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Goal: student `model_request`, line 1 | Reconstruct a 512 × 384 indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching camera, framing, colors, placement and materials. The student’s “woodworking tool shop” interpretation is an inference, not independently verified scene content. |
| Initial build: student `model_response` line 3; `execute` step 1 line 4 | Code specified walls, window, shelves, bench, many tools and containers. It grouped plane bodies, blades and handles as assets and rotated objects into different poses. Wood/metal-like colors, roughness and bevels were specified; no image textures are evident. Grouping and coordinates do not independently verify physical connections or correct placement. |
| Camera and failure: lines 4–5 | The program set a camera, three area lights and Cycles settings. Step 1 failed with `AttributeError` because `scene.world` was `None`; `image` was null. Thus no visual comparison was possible from that execution. |
| Revision: student `model_request` line 6; `model_response` line 8; `execute` step 2 line 9 | The runner supplied the traceback to the student. The revised program created and assigned a node-based world, and also altered the saw rail and side-plane placement. The same camera and area-light arrangement remained. The revision was actually executed, not merely proposed. |
| Validation: `execution_result` line 10, characters [0,185899); `select` line 11 | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, logged many synchronized mesh objects and saved `final.png` and `scene.blend`; step 2 was selected. The log reports 16 render samples despite the program setting 48. Execution success is not visual or geometric verification. |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposal, input or adoption is visible in this chunk. The traceback was runner feedback, not teacher advice. The student independently produced and revised code; the two recorded student CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 7). No separate autonomous search or visual review is visible here.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The first attempt experienced a technical execution failure; the second achieved a successful build/render and selection. Overall task correctness and final outcome remain **unknown**: neither image is available for comparison, and later chunks are outside scope. In particular, reference fidelity, object occlusion, part contact, pose, camera framing, lighting and material appearance remain unresolved hypotheses—not established defects or successes.

**Lessons.** Transferably, distinguish a successful render from a verified reconstruction, and use concrete runtime feedback to diagnose initialization errors. The missing Blender world and the chosen shop geometry are specific to this attempt; the visible record does not establish whether the modeled scene matched the photograph.
